sections.h2: What does the Arkansas landscape mean for a home seller?
sections.html:
Arkansas covers about 52,000 square miles of land and counted 3,011,524 residents in the 2020 census, which works out to roughly 58 people per square mile. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 3,114,791, an increase of 3.4% over the 2020 base.

The Arkansas Geological Survey divides the state into five physiographic regions: the Ozark Plateaus, the Arkansas River Valley, the Ouachita Mountains, the West Gulf Coastal Plain and the Mississippi River Alluvial Plain. The National Park Service describes the Boston Mountains as the boundary between the Ozark and Ouachita provinces, with the Arkansas Valley as a lowland across the north of the Ouachita province. Crowley's Ridge, a belt of sand and gravel under windblown soil, rises in the east.

For a seller, the practical point is that a house in the Delta lowlands, one in the hills of the northwest and one in a Little Rock suburb sit in very different local conditions, yet all of them go through the same state tax and recording machinery described below.

sections.h2: Where are the largest property markets in Arkansas?
sections.html:
The population is concentrated in a few counties and cities, and the growth rates differ sharply.

  • Pulaski County holds Little Rock and had an estimated 404,611 residents in July 2025. Little Rock itself counted 202,591 in the 2020 census, up from 193,524 in 2010.
  • Benton County had 284,333 residents in the 2020 base and an estimate of 332,554 in 2025, a 17.0% gain in five years, against 3.4% for the whole state.
  • Washington County counted 245,871 in 2020 and has grown about 10.3% since. Fayetteville, its largest city, counted 93,949 in 2020, up from 73,580 in 2010.

Rapid growth shows up in assessments. Benton County's assessor has already announced a countywide reappraisal for 2028, and a house sold in a fast-moving county can be revalued soon after the sale, as the property tax section explains.

sections.h2: How is property tax run in Arkansas?
sections.html:
Each county assessor values real estate, the county collector bills it, and the state's Assessment Coordination Division sets the rules. Property is assessed at 20% of market value, and the tax equals that assessed value times the millage rate for the taxing districts the property sits in. Clark County's assessor notes that school millage is set by election each year, while the governing bodies set county and city rates.

Assessors do not wait for owners to report. The Department of Finance and Administration says real property is assessed each year to the owner of record, and owners should report new buildings, additions or a change in use, such as moving from owner-occupied to rental. Values are reset during a reappraisal that runs on a three, four or five year cycle, and Amendment 79 requires reassessment at least every five years.

Arkansas bills taxes in arrears. The Benton County assessor explains that a 2026 assessment is billed in spring 2027 and paid by October 15, 2027. Statements usually arrive in the spring, and Faulkner County's collector tells owners to call if one has not come by July 1.

sections.h2: When are Arkansas property taxes due, and how can an assessment be appealed?
sections.html:
Taxes are payable to the county collector by October 15 each year, moving to the next business day when that date falls on a weekend or legal holiday. Craighead County's collector says taxes unpaid after October 15 draw a 10% penalty, and Faulkner County adds 10% annual interest on delinquent real estate taxes.

An owner who disagrees with a value should first call the county assessor, since errors in the property record can often be fixed without a formal appeal. For larger disputes, the state says the last day to schedule a hearing with the county Board of Equalization is the third Monday in August.

Two statewide protections help owners who live in their house. The homestead tax credit is worth up to $675 a year according to the 2026 report of the Assessment Coordination Division, and homestead values can rise no more than 5% a year after a reappraisal, against 10% for other real property. Our homestead page covers who qualifies and what happens to these benefits on a sale.

sections.h2: What state taxes and recording steps apply when a house is sold?
sections.html:
Arkansas charges a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of actual consideration on transactions above $100. The Department of Finance and Administration administers it through transfer stamps, with an affidavit of compliance form and a stamp-change request form for corrections, and the tax statute is Ark. Code § 26-60-101 and following.

Deeds are recorded at the county level. In Arkansas counties, the circuit clerk also acts as the ex officio recorder, responsible for recording deeds, mortgages, liens and surety bonds. A seller therefore deals with two county offices after a closing: the circuit clerk for the recorded deed and the assessor for the ownership change on the tax roll.

The assessor's response to a sale can surprise a buyer. Under Ark. Code § 26-26-1123, the property is assessed at 20% of its appraised value at the next assessment date after title transfers, and a buyer cannot claim an assessment limit until the second assessment date afterward.

sections.h2: How do foreclosure and delinquent taxes work in Arkansas?
sections.html:
Arkansas lenders can foreclose without a court case under the Statutory Foreclosure Act, though the lender may still choose a judicial foreclosure. Section 18-50-116 states that the statutory procedure does not impair the right to bring a judicial action. Under § 18-50-104, a notice of default and intention to sell must be mailed by certified mail within 30 days after the notice is recorded, and it must state the time, date and place of sale along with the name and contact details of the party starting the foreclosure.

The Attorney General urges owners who receive a default notice to call the servicer right away, to ignore anyone who asks to take over the deed in exchange for saving the house, and to use free HUD-approved counselors, who can be reached at (800) 569-4287. Act 885 of 2011 directs servicers to share loss mitigation contacts before a foreclosure.

Unpaid property taxes lead to a different path. Counties certify delinquent parcels to the Commissioner of State Lands, and once certified the legal title vests in the state. An owner can redeem the parcel until the deadline before the auction, and the Real Estate Division in Little Rock, at 1020 W. 4th Street, handles payment.

sections.h2: How do landlord and tenant rules differ in Arkansas?
sections.html: Arkansas lets a landlord pursue unpaid rent through a civil suit or a criminal charge. Little Rock's housing department says Arkansas is the only state with a criminal eviction statute, and unpaid rent can lead to a civil unlawful detainer case after three days' written notice. Deposits are capped at two months' rent only for landlords who rent six or more dwellings. Owners selling a rented house should read the state guides on eviction and tenant rights before promising a buyer a vacant property.

faqs.q: How many people live in Arkansas?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 3,011,524 people. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 3,114,791, which is 3.4% above the 2020 base.

faqs.q: What is the Arkansas real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of actual consideration on transactions above $100, collected through stamps on the deed and administered by the Department of Finance and Administration.

faqs.q: When are Arkansas property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 15 each year, payable to the county collector. If that date falls on a weekend or holiday, the due date moves to the next business day, and the first bill for a given assessment year arrives the following spring.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in Arkansas?
faqs.a: The circuit clerk of the county where the property sits, who serves as ex officio recorder. The clerk records deeds, mortgages, liens and other instruments involving county property.

faqs.q: Does Arkansas foreclose through the courts?
faqs.a: Not always. The Statutory Foreclosure Act allows a lender to sell after proper notice without a lawsuit, though a lender may still choose a judicial foreclosure under § 18-50-116.

faqs.q: What is the Arkansas homestead credit worth?
faqs.a: Up to $675 a year on a principal residence, according to the Assessment Coordination Division's 2026 annual report and county assessors. The owner applies with the county assessor.
